subject: Enclave + sidecar: isolation, attack scenarios, and evidence packet

Subject: Enclave/sidecar isolation — follow-up to RFI

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. As we work through our vendor assessment for Granite Systems, the reviewers asked for a concise summary of the runtime isolation and network egress controls for Redwood's enclave+sidecar deployment. Specific asks:

- A network diagram showing data/control plane demarcation, sidecar boundaries, and permitted egress paths.
- A short threat summary describing the top 5 plausible lateral movement / data-exfiltration scenarios and mitigations.
- Evidence/artifacts (config snippets, proof of routing ACLs, telemetry examples) we can include in our security pack.

Can you send a single packet we can circulate to our auditors today? Our target review meeting is Monday morning (US-Eastern).

—Jordan
Granite Systems — InfoSec

[No attachments in this message]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Meyers <security@granite-sys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 09:12:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Enclave/sidecar isolation — follow-up to RFI

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear list. Attaching a focused packet that addresses each bullet. High level summary up-front:

- Isolation model: customer inference workloads run in a tenant-specific enclave (kernel & network namespace isolation) with a per-tenant sidecar that terminates requests and enforces egress ACLs. Control plane (model management, orchestration) runs in a separate management VPC with strictly one-way, authenticated polling for telemetry.

- Network demarcation: data plane (inference traffic) is confined to sealed subnets; sidecars are the only path to egress. Inter-enclave communication is disabled by default; where telemetry is required we use a managed forwarder in a dedicated telemetry subnet with mTLS and per-tenant credentials.

- Threat summary: included are four prioritized attack scenarios (privileged container breakout, compromised operator key, misconfigured egress ACL, supply-chain model poisoning) with mitigations and detectable signals.

Attachments: network-diagram-v3.png (annotated topology), enclave-evidence-bundle.pdf (config snippets + ACL export + telemetry sample), attack-matrix-annotated.xlsx (scenario severity + detection controls).

We kept the packet compact for auditor consumption; Ben and Marissa are looped in for any deeper artifacts you need. If you prefer a single-page executive summary for Monday, we can produce that by EOD PST.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference
[e: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai | m: +1 (415) 555-0182]

Subject: Re: Enclave/sidecar isolation — follow-up to RFI

Jordan / team —

Quick clarifications from the runtime side to help your auditors:

1) Sidecar egress enforcement: sidecars are configured with iptables rules generated from a per-tenant ACL store; those rules are deployed atomically and signed by the control plane. You can find an exported ACL sample in the attached PDF (lines 42-57 show the allow list for telemetry endpoints).

2) KV cache and shared artifacts: the runtime uses a read-only blob store for model artifacts with signed manifests; replicas are mounted read-only in the enclave. No writeable shared filesystem is exposed to tenant workloads.

3) Telemetry & detection: we push sampled flow logs and per-request telemetry to the telemetry forwarder over mTLS; the forwarder strips tenant ids from payloads for privacy but retains request digests for anomaly detection.

I added two short notes into the attack matrix (column G) explaining expected alerting behavior and a suggested auditor query for flow logs (also included in the evidence bundle).

—Ben
Ben Carter — Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jordan —

Following up with a short checklist and suggested auditor queries to speed review:

1) Review packet contents: network-diagram-v3.png (confirm sealed subnet paths), enclave-evidence-bundle.pdf (look at ACL export + systemd unit hashes), attack-matrix-annotated.xlsx (scenarios + detection).

2) Suggested queries for your auditor (examples included in the evidence bundle):
   - flow_log.search("tenant_id:GRT-20345 AND dest_ip:10.12.0.0/16 AND action:ALLOW")
   - telemetry.events("auth_failure") | where(source=="sidecar")

3) Next steps: if the auditor requests runtime captures (pcap snippets or real-time ACL diffs), we can provide a timeboxed capture with a signed digest for verification. Note that all captures are redacted to remove other tenants' metadata.

I'll produce a one-page executive summary and an SSO link to the evidence folder for your reviewers before close of business PST; Evelyn, Ben — let me know if you'd like any last edits.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Security Operations, Redwood Inference
